1315.question: A Filipino while residing abroad purchased a vehicle the design and cost of which is appropriate for his position and standing. He returned to the Philippines under the “returning resident” scheme for conditionally free importation entry for the vehicle. May the vehicle enter conditionally free in as much as the Filipino is a returning resident?

choices.A: Yes, but Certificate of Authority to Import (CAI) must be secured from Fair Trade Enforcement Bureau (FTEB).
choices.B: Yes, but only in so far as the customs duty for the car is concerned. Excise tax will have to be paid.
choices.C: No, because vehicles are not covered by the conditionally free importation for returning residents.
choices.D: Yes, but the car should pass LTO safety considerations.

1318.question: S/S “Malumay” a vessel of Philippine registry while docked at Port of Singapore encountered mechanical problems. The Captain of the vessel contracted a Singaporean engineer to repair the vessel. The total cost of the repair is twenty five thousand dolars (US$25,000.00) broken down as follows: US$20,000.00 for materials and US$5,000.00 for labor. What shall be the tax treatment of total cost of repair assuming that the repair may enter conditionally free?

choices.A: US$25,000.00 total will enter conditionally free.
choices.B: US$20,000.00 cost of materials will enter conditionally free.
choices.C: US$5,000.00 cost of labor will enter conditionally free.
choices.D: Any of the above is correct depending on the value of the vessel.

1318.note: CMTA Sec. 800(c): the conditionally-free item is 'Cost of repairs, EXCLUDING the value of the goods used.' Only the labor/repair cost is exempt; the value of materials/parts remains dutiable. So the $5,000 labor portion enters conditionally free, not the $20,000 in materials.

1339.question: An equipment was sent abroad for repair after compliance with procedures under Section 800 of CMTA. After repair the equipment was returned to the Philippines through consolidated shipment and covered by a HBL. To repair the equipment some old screws were replaced at a cost of US$100.00, the stand of the equipment was also replaced at a cost of US$200.00 and cost of labor amounted to US$200.00. How shall the customs duty be computed?

choices.A: The importation shall be treated as duty free under the provisions of Section 800 of CMTA.
choices.B: Customs duty shall be imposed based on DV of US$300.00- value of screws and stand and tariff heading to be used is for screws and for stand.
choices.C: Customs duty shall be imposed based on DV of US$500.00 and tariff heading to be used is for there repaired equipment.
choices.D: Customs duty shall be imposed only on the cost of labor of US$200.00 and duty rate shall be 30%.

1339.note: Same Sec. 800(c) principle: value of parts used (screws + stand = US$300) is excluded from the exemption and is what's dutiable; only labor is conditionally free.

1345.question: A Philippine registered vessel engaged in foreign trade has undergone an emergency repair abroad and some parts of her engine have to be replaced. What is the tax treatment of the total cost of repair?

choices.A: Both cost of labor of the repair and replaced parts are duty and tax free.
choices.B: Only the cost of the parts that replaced the defective parts of the vessel shall enter duty and tax free
choices.C: Only the cost of labor of the repair shall not be subject to payment of duty and tax.
choices.D: It depends on the total cost of repair

1345.note: Same Sec. 800(c) principle: only the cost of LABOR is conditionally duty/tax-free; the value of replacement parts is not.

1347.question: If an importation of books exceeds the number to be considered as for personal use, what should be secured for the books to enter duty and tax free?

1348.question: Mr. “A” went to the United States last June 2025 to enjoy Disneyland. Upon his arrival at NAIA last July 5, 2025 the examination of his baggage showed new personal and household effects valued at US$2,000.00 which “A” declared as “pasalubongs” for his family. Is he exempt from payment of duties and taxes on the US$2,000.00 personal and household effects?

choices.A: Yes, even if it exceeds the de minimis value.
choices.B: No, as he is a returning resident.
choices.C: No, as he is not a qualified Filipino.
choices.D: Yes, as he is not considered as an OFW

1349.question: An OFW from Italy went to Rome Freight Forwarding and sent 1 package to her husband, 1 package for her daughter and 1 package for her son. The shipment is covered by one MAWB and 3 HAWB. How many BBB availment is this?

choices.C: One if the total amount of the packages does not exceed P150,000.00
choices.D: Three if the total amount of the package is P150,000.00

1350.question: A returning resident brought with him a car which has been registered under his name for ten (10) years. May the car enter duty and tax free under the provisions of CMTA?

choices.A: Yes, but the value of the car should not exceed P350,000.00 and he has already stayed abroad for 10 years as evidenced by the registration of the car in his name.
choices.B: Yes, but a Certificate of Authority to Import (CAI) must be secured from FTEB
choices.C: Yes, but duties and taxes must be paid and CAI should be secured from LTO

1401.question: If a Filipino national stayed in a foreign country for a period of five (5) years what is the maximum value of personal and household effects that he may bring with him upon his return that may enter conditionally free?

choices.A: Three Hundred Fifty Thousand Pesos (P350,000.00) FOB or FCA.
choices.B: Two Hundred Fifty Thousand Pesos (P250,000.00) FOB or FCA.
choices.C: One Hundred Fifty Thousand Pesos (P150,000.00) FOB or FCA.

1402.question: Which of the following choices has the authority to suspend disallow or completely withdraw, in whole or in part a conditionally free importation under CMTA, Section 800?

choices.A: Commissioner of Customs subject to approval of the Secretary of Finance.
choices.B: District Collector subject to approval of the Commissioner of Customs.
choices.D: President of the Philippines upon the recommendation of the Secretary of Finance.

1403.question: Who are not qualified to send balikbayan boxes?

choices.B: Filipino resident national studying in Harvard University.
choices.C: Filipino tourists in Wuhan, China on two (2) days tour only.
choices.D: All of the above are qualified to send balikbayan boxes.

1404.question: Who are not qualified as recipients of balikbayan boxes?

choices.D: All are qualified to receive balikbayan boxes.

1405.question: What is the re-exportation period for goods used exclusively for public entertainment, and for display in public expositions, or for exhibition or competition for prizes, and devices for projecting pictures and appurtenances?

choices.B: Three (3) months but may be extended for another three (3) months,
choices.D: Six (6) months but may be extended for another six (6) months.

1406.question: Importations for the official use of foreign embassies, legations and other agencies of foreign governments qualify for conditionally free importation if a certain condition is met. What is that condition?

choices.A: The foreign countries accord like privileges to corresponding agencies of the Philippines.
choices.B: Importation of vehicle must be brand new.
choices.C: The foreign countries are members of the United Nations.

1407.question: Goods and salvage from vessels recovered after a period of two (2) years from the date of filing the marine protest or the time when the vessel was wrecked or abandoned in Philippine waters or elsewhere, or parts of a foreign vessel or its equipment, wrecked or abandoned in Philippine waters or elsewhere may be considered as conditionally free importation. Is the statement correct?

choices.A: No, because the salvaged goods are still subject to payment of duties and taxes.
choices.B: Yes, but as provided for under the IRR a Certificate of Origin must be presented by the importer who claims the salvaged goods.
choices.C: No, because the statement is contrary to law.
choices.D: Yes, as provided for under CMTA.

1408.question: Goods sold or used for purposes other than intended without prior payment of duties shall be:

1409.question: Which is an exception to forfeiture when duty-free goods are disposed of?

1410.question: Duty-free importations generally require which document from the DOF?

1413.question: VAT and excise tax exemption require issuance of:

1419.question: Security required for temporarily admitted goods is usually:

1421.question: Goods brought into the Philippines for repair, processing or reconditioning to be re-exported upon completion of the or reconditioning may enter repair, processing conditionally free provided that the goods are re-exported after a certain period of time. What is re-exportation period?

choices.A: Six (6) months from discharge from carrying vessel.
choices.B: Three (3) months from acceptance of goods declaration which may be extended for another three (3) months.
choices.C: Six (6) months from acceptance of goods declaration.
choices.D: Six (6) months from acceptance of goods declaration the period of which may be extended for another six (6) months for valid reasons.

1424.question: Which of the following choices shall prescribe the regulations that must be complied with in order to avail of conditionally tax and/or duty exempt importation?

choices.A: Secretary of Finance and Secretary of Trade and Industry.
choices.C: Commissioner of Customs subject to joint approval of Secretary of Finance and Secretary of Trade and Industry.
choices.D: Commissioner of Customs subject to approval of the Secretary of Finance.

1424.note: CMTA Sec. 800, opening paragraph: formalities are 'promulgated by the Commissioner with the approval of the Secretary of Finance' only — the Secretary of Trade and Industry is not part of this approval chain.

1425.question: If scientific and technical films imported conditionally free by technical and scientific institutions are exhibited for profit what shall be the corresponding penalty?

choices.A: Proceeds shall be subject to confiscation.
choices.C: Confiscation of proceeds and forfeiture of films.
choices.D: Any of the above as determined by the Commissioner of Customs.

1429.question: To qualify as conditionally free importation aquatic goods caught must not have been landed in any foreign territory. If landed for what purpose only?

choices.A: For canning purposes so that the goods will not spoil during transit.
choices.C: For purposes of changing the registry of the gathering vessel into Philippine registry.

1429.note: CMTA Sec. 800(a): aquatic products must not have been landed in foreign territory, 'or, if so landed, that they have been landed solely for TRANSSHIPMENT' — not canning. Since 'transshipment' isn't one of the 4 options, none of A/B/C is correct.

1430.question: Under CMTA, Section 800(b) there are conditions to be complied with so that equipment for use in the salvage of vessels or aircrafts may enter conditionally free. Which of the following is not among the conditions?

choices.A: The equipment is not locally available.
choices.B: Certificate of Identification is secured at the time of importation.
choices.C: Posting of security in the amount of one hundred fifty percent (150%) of the ascertained duties and taxes.
choices.D: All of the above are conditions under CMTA, Section 800(b)

1433.question: Balikbayan boxes are exempt up to how many times per year?

1434.question: What is the condition as to the period of stay of a Filipino national in a foreign country before he may be considered as a “returning resident”?

choices.A: The Filipino national should have stayed in a foreign country for at least one (1) year.
choices.B: The Filipino national should have stayed in a foreign country for at least six (6) months.
choices.C: The Filipino national should have stayed in a foreign country for at least nine (9) months.
choices.D: Any of the above depending on the value of the goods to be brought in by the Filipino national

1435.question: In addition to the privileges granted as returning residents, returning Overseas Filipino Workers (OFWs) shall have the privilege to bring in, tax and duty free, home appliances and other durables. What are the limitations to this privilege?

choices.A: It shall be limited to one of every kind.
choices.B: May be availed only once in a given calendar year.
choices.C: Must accompany the OFW or must arrive within a reasonable time which shall not exceed sixty (60) days from return of the OFW.

1436.question: Total value limit of Balikbayan boxes per year:

1437.question: How shall the maximum amount of appliances that may be brought in by an OFW conditionally free be adjusted?

choices.A: District Collector shall adjust the value every three (3) years from CMTA effectivity based on CPI as published by PSA.
choices.B: Commissioner of Customs subject to approval of the Secretary of Finance adjust the value every three (3) years from CMTA effectivity based on CPI as published by PSA.
choices.C: The Secretary of Finance shall adjust the value every three (3) years from CMTA effectivity based on CPI as published by PSA.
choices.D: It depends based on CMTA IRR that may be promulgated.

1439.question: What is the maximum number of times that qualified Filipinos and OFWs are allowed to send baikbayan boxes?

choices.A: Maximum of three (3) times per calendar year.
choices.B: Maximum of one (1) every four (4) months.
choices.C: It depends on the qualified Filipinos or OFWs.
choices.D: Any of the choice is correct

1440.question: Are vehicles included in the conditionally free importation privilege of persons coming to settle to the Philippines?

choices.A: Yes, but the vehicle must be brand new.
choices.B: Yes, but the vehicle must have been registered in the name of the person coming to settle.

1441.question: May ATA Carnets be accepted for hand-carried and unaccompanied goods?

choices.A: No, as ATA Carnets may only cover commercial goods.
choices.B: No, as ATA Carnets may only cover big items.
choices.C: No, as a matter of regulation.
choices.D: Yes, as a matter of regulation

1441.note: Per CAO 02-2022 (BOC's ATA Carnet implementing rules): 'ATA Carnets are accepted for hand-carried goods and unaccompanied goods' (they are NOT accepted only for postal traffic and customs transit).

1442.question: What is the maximum liability of the National Issuing and Guaranteeing Association (NIGA)?

choices.A: Not more than the amount of duties and taxes due on the guaranteed goods.
choices.B: Not more than the value of the goods being guaranteed.
choices.C: Not more than 110% of the duties and taxes due on the guaranteed goods.
choices.D: Not more than 110% of the value of the goods being guaranteed.

1443.question: ATA Carnet may replace which document?

1444.question: The maximum validity of an ATA Carnet issued by the NIGA?

choices.A: Maximum is equal to the required re-exportation period of the goods temporarily admitted.
choices.C: Six (6) months subject to extension by another six (6) months.
